title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Essay Structure
summary: The 4-paragraph structure that scores Band 7+ on Task 2, and how to plan it in 5 minutes.

nodes.label: Introduction
nodes.note: Paraphrase the question + clear thesis (your position)

nodes.label: Body 1
nodes.note: First main idea → explain → one specific example

nodes.label: Body 2
nodes.note: Second main idea → explain → one specific example

nodes.label: Conclusion
nodes.note: Restate your position; add no new ideas

chunks.heading: Introduction: paraphrase + thesis
chunks.body: Rewrite the question in your own words (don't copy it), then state your **position** in one clear sentence. Examiners look for a thesis they can find in 5 seconds.
chunks.realExample: Question: 'Some think exams are the best way to assess students.' Intro thesis: 'While exams measure knowledge under pressure, I believe continuous assessment gives a fairer overall picture.'
chunks.memoryHook: PT = Paraphrase, then Thesis. Two sentences, no more.

chunks.heading: Body paragraphs: one idea each
chunks.body: Each body paragraph = **one** main idea, an explanation of *why* it matters, and **one specific example**. Two focused paragraphs beat one crowded one.
chunks.realExample: Body idea: 'Continuous assessment reduces exam anxiety.' Example: 'A 2019 UK pilot found coursework-based grading cut reported student stress by a third.'
chunks.memoryHook: IEE: Idea → Explain → Example. Say it out loud before you write.

chunks.heading: Conclusion: restate, don't add
chunks.body: Summarise your position in one or two sentences. **Never** introduce a new argument in the conclusion — it costs you Coherence marks.
chunks.realExample: 'Overall, although exams have their place, a mix of continuous assessment and exams assesses students more fairly.'
chunks.memoryHook: A conclusion is a mirror, not a window: it reflects what you said, it doesn't open new views.

chunks.heading: Plan in 5 minutes
chunks.body: Spend 5 of your 40 minutes planning: decide your position, jot one idea + example per body paragraph. Planning is the single biggest predictor of a coherent essay.
chunks.realExample: Scribble: 'Pos: mix is fairer | B1: anxiety (UK pilot) | B2: measures different skills (creativity)'. That's a whole essay mapped.
chunks.memoryHook: 5 to plan, 30 to write, 5 to check. 5-30-5.

recall.q: How many sentences should a Task 2 introduction be, and what are they?
recall.a: Two: a paraphrase of the question, then a clear thesis stating your position.

recall.q: What three parts make up a good body paragraph?
recall.a: One main idea, an explanation of why it matters, and one specific example (IEE).

recall.q: What must you never do in the conclusion?
recall.a: Introduce a new argument or idea — only restate your position.

recall.q: How should you split your 40 minutes on Task 2?
Why is paraphrasing the question important?
recall.a: Copying the question wording scores zero for that text and signals weak vocabulary; paraphrasing shows range.
